about: Which tool has a documented, first-class way to do each block of work, on the CPU and on the GPU. A cell is covered only when the tool's own documentation shows a designed feature or API for it, not a workaround (masking every lane, writing raw CUDA strings inside it, running the slowest sample to the end). 'judgement' marks a cell the author found close to the line. Performance is not part of this table.

blocks.handtuned: You write what each thread does and how it is launched.
blocks.fixed: Many independent ODEs stepped with a fixed step.
blocks.deriv: Derivatives of a result with respect to its inputs, generated for you.
blocks.zerocopy: Arrays handed to and from other libraries without a copy (DLPack or the CUDA array interface).
blocks.models: You write one sample's model; the batching is done for you.
blocks.half: float16 or bfloat16 arithmetic as a supported path.
blocks.linalg: Dense linear algebra and large solvers as library calls.
blocks.ensembles: Many independent samples in one run, with random numbers per sample.
blocks.divergent: Samples that diverge keep the hardware busy, without masking every lane or waiting for the slowest one.
blocks.events: A sample stops on its own condition and stops costing work.
blocks.adaptive: Each sample picks its own step size from an embedded error estimate.
blocks.deploy: A compiled program runs from C++ or another runtime, without Python.
blocks.diffsim: Gradients through a whole simulation, into a training loop.
blocks.datagen: Simulated batches handed to a training framework without copies.
blocks.hybrid: A network and a physics model in one differentiable program.
blocks.training: Training dense tensor models: layers, optimisers, training loops.
blocks.inference: Inference in low precision, such as bfloat16, float8 or quantised integers.

handtuned.why: Raw thread-level control belongs to simulation code, far from neural networks.

models.why: Writing one sample's model and letting the library batch it is the simulation way.

ensembles.why: Monte Carlo ensembles are simulation, close to statistics.

adaptive.why: Embedded-pair step control is numerical simulation.

divergent.why: Divergent samples come from simulation, and also shape batched learning data.

half.why: Half precision is shared: simulation can use it, learning leans on it.

diffsim.why: Gradients through a simulation sit at the join of the two sides.

deriv.why: Generated derivatives serve simulation sensitivities and training alike.

events.why: A sample that stops on its own condition is a simulation idea that learning loops borrow.

deploy.why: Running outside Python serves simulation runs and trained models alike.

datagen.why: Simulated data feeding a training loop sits between the two.

linalg.why: Dense linear algebra serves solvers and networks alike.

zerocopy.why: Zero-copy hand-over connects simulation arrays to learning frameworks.

hybrid.why: A network and a physics model in one program, leaning to the AI side.

arraystyle.why: Whole-array programs are the usual way neural code is written.

training.why: Training dense tensor models is the AI side.

inference.why: Low-precision inference is the AI side.

y_about: Per tool and capability: -1 = CPU only (top band), 0 = CPU and GPU (middle band), +1 = GPU only (bottom band), null = not first-class. Graded values in between may be stored later.

radar_axes.about: Each judged (qualitative) radar axis and the capability row that shows the same claim. A score of 4 or more needs the capability covered on at least one device; a covered capability must not score 2 or less.

tensor.why: Dense tensor work is the dense linear algebra and large-solver row.

array_style.why: Whole-array expressions are the array-style row.

half_precision.why: Half precision and below is the half-precision row.

control.why: Writing what each thread does is the hand-tuned kernels row.

single_thread.why: Writing one sample is the per-sample models row.

differentiable.why: Built-in derivatives are the differentiable sensitivities row.

arrays.why: Zero-copy exchange with other frameworks is the zero-copy hand-over row.

deploy.why: A compiled program that runs without Python is the deployment row.

extensible.why: A plugin path across targets has no capability row, so it is judged on the rubric alone.
